The Challenger exploded at 11:39 am. I was at university, and at lunch I heard a half-dozen Challenger jokes. I think the thing to do is to recognize that most folks telling these jokes mean no ill will to the victims, and that it's simple human nature.

It's a coping mechanism. My grandmother died about two months ago. She used to call the house often and talk to whomever happened to be home. Many times it was my step dad. My step dad died about five years ago.

Not an hour after my grandmother had passed I look over at my sister and go "I bet step dad (used his name) is getting an ear full right now." She looked perplexed for just a second then it dawned on her and she just started laughing. We all thought it was hilarious how he'd always end up talking to her for like an hour on the phone a couple times a week, but he took it well.

Either way point being that it's a good thing, not all will see it as that, but we all deal with tragedy in our own ways.

I tried not to go with the coping mechanism explanation because I'm not a mental health professional nor a mind reader. I'm certain that in many cases it is about coping, or about reducing the stress of the issue. Or maybe it's just a power grab for an easy shock-value joke. I think the important point is really that in virtually all cases there is no actual malice intended - it's just a joke. It doesn't hurt anyone, and whatever the intent, it can certainly have the effect of normalizing the issue so everyone can get on with their lives.

And for anyone "triggered" by the jokes, all I can say is man the fuck up. Life is pain - deal with it or get the fuck out of my way.
